title: Virginia Orders Data Centers To Pay for Dedicated New Electric Infrastructure
excerpt: The governor said in a statement the move could save Virginia ratepayers "hundreds of millions of dollars."
content_html:
Virginia, home of the nation's densest concentration of data centers, will require them to pay for the dedicated new power infrastructure they need in a bid to spare homeowners from rising electric bills.

The commonwealth's State Corporation Commission ordered large data center users to cover the cost of transmission infrastructure they will use exclusively.

Gov. Abigail Spanberger recently pushed for developers to offset their impact on the power grid. Across the nation, residents blame rising energy costs, in part, on a rapid build-out of the large technology developments.

That includes substations, electric lines, and other electric infrastructure "upstream" from the data center sites. The governor said in a statement the move could save Virginia ratepayers "hundreds of millions of dollars."

"We are taking real steps to address rising energy costs for Virginians," Spanberger said. "I will continue to work with the General Assembly and take action to make sure data centers pay their fair share, adhere to strict environmental standards, and listen to the concerns of local communities.”

'Data Center Alley' contends with growth

The state is home to at least 570 data centers, thanks in part to its "Data Center Alley" in Northern Virginia, which takes advantage of infrastructure that dates to the creation of the internet.

But the speed and scope of data centers have been controversial with residents. Goldman Sachs estimated that data center power demand will more than double from 2025 to 2027. But only about 50% to 60% of data center capacity will come online due to delays and cancellations, it said.

The National Association of Home Builders highlighted the data center–dense Northern Virginia suburbs as an area where data centers might be outbidding homebuilders and adding a new struggle to the housing market.

The state's DC suburbs, which account for a third of its population, have seen median prices go up 54% over the past decade, the Northern Virginia Association of Realtors found.

In a statement to Realtor.com®, the Data Center Coalition, which represents many major developers and users in the industry, said companies operate how they are authorized to do so.

They also follow local ordinances and rules. And they provided 5.5 million jobs, $204 billion in taxes, and $1.7 trillion in gross domestic product, said Nicole Riley, director of Virginia Government Affairs for the group.

"The industry is committed to working with local, state, regional, and federal regulators and policymakers, as well as Virginia residents, to promote the continued responsible development of this industry that is critical to Virginia’s 21st-century economy," Riley said.

Tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

content_html_zh:
弗吉尼亚州是全国数据中心最密集的地区，将要求他们支付所需的专用新电力基础设施费用，以避免房主承受不断上涨的电费。

联邦国家公司委员会命令大型数据中心用户承担他们专门使用的传输基础设施的成本。

政府。 阿比盖尔·斯潘伯格最近敦促开发商抵消其对电网的影响。 全国各地的居民将能源成本上涨部分归咎于大型技术发展的快速发展。

这包括变电站、电线和数据中心站点“上游”的其他电力基础设施。 州长在一份声明中表示，此举可以为弗吉尼亚州纳税人节省“数亿美元”。

斯潘伯格说：“我们正在采取切实措施来解决弗吉尼亚人不断上涨的能源成本问题。” “我将继续与大会合作，采取行动确保数据中心支付公平的份额，遵守严格的环境标准，并倾听当地社区的担忧。”

“数据中心胡同”与增长作斗争

该州拥有至少 570 个数据中心，部分归功于弗吉尼亚州北部的“数据中心巷”，它利用了自互联网诞生以来的基础设施。

但数据中心的速度和范围一直引起居民的争议。 高盛预计，从 2025 年到 2027 年，数据中心的电力需求将增加一倍以上。 但由于延误和取消，只有约 50% 至 60% 的数据中心容量能够上线。

全国住宅建筑商协会强调，在数据中心密集的弗吉尼亚州北部郊区，数据中心的出价可能会高于住宅建筑商，并给房地产市场带来新的挑战。

北弗吉尼亚州房地产经纪人协会发现，该州的 DC 郊区占该州人口的三分之一，过去十年中房价中位数上涨了 54%。

代表该行业许多主要开发商和用户的数据中心联盟在向 Realtor.com® 发表的一份声明中表示，各公司按照其授权的方式运营。

他们还遵守当地的法令和规则。 该组织弗吉尼亚州政府事务总监 Nicole Riley 表示，它们提供了 550 万个就业岗位、2040 亿美元的税收和 1.7 万亿美元的国内生产总值。

赖利说：“该行业致力于与地方、州、地区和联邦监管机构和政策制定者以及弗吉尼亚州居民合作，促进该行业持续负责任的发展，这对弗吉尼亚州的 21 世纪经济至关重要。”

特里斯坦·纳维拉 (Tristan Navera) 是住房政策领域的资深记者，报道华盛顿特区住房市场的趋势和解决方案。 他此前曾担任彭博社法律部的高级记者，此前曾为《华盛顿商业日报》报道房地产。 在他职业生涯的早期，他花了十年时间报道俄亥俄州代顿和哥伦布的商业和房地产。 他是辛辛那提人，拥有俄亥俄大学新闻学学位。
